terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Near frontal illustration; camera fit remains to be confirmed from actual browser captures. +Z front, Y-up. Fixed review is frontal; orbit views are volume evidence, not matched references.

objectClass.primaryType: anime humanoid learning companion, Hatsune Miku reference outfit
objectClass.notes: User selected reference-proportioned stylized cartoon reconstruction, with inferred hidden sides, then static user review before animation.

reasoning: Two hip-length broad spline-loft ponytails dominate lateral silhouette.
Unified head, fitted garment shell, pleated skirt, flared sleeves and long boots require different surface strategies.
Paired limbs, fingers and hairstyle layers require named contact and future pivots; animation remains pending user static acceptance.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Major body/head/hair/outfit assemblies, repeated bangs and skirt pleats, palette-specific trim/details and separate rear review.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

anatomy.note: Pixel guide overlay inspected by agent; body proportions are reference estimates, not generic canon. Reference ornament tips are excluded from skull HH; rear depth inferred under user accepted stylization.

definitionOfDone: Reference-proportioned stylized Miku remains recognizable from full-body and head views: teal eyes, high-root broad long twin tails, white fitted blouse, cyan tie/trim, dark flared sleeves, pleated skirt and thigh boots.
Static preview renders a genuine volumetric model from frontal, ±35°, profile, rear-three-quarter and rear cameras; user must accept static appearance before animation.
No false claims of recovered back geometry, physical PBR, skin deformation or animation readiness.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match

stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Source is a flat-shaded 2D illustration, not a measured material photograph; textureless base-color declarations are evidence-bearing, facial artwork projection is treated as albedo graphics, never as recovered PBR. Reference visual fidelity is reviewed in browser.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Single-view stylized reconstruction accepted in Q2; rear and profile are inferred, not observations.
Static preview phase only; all rigging, skinning, expression animation and motion clips remain unimplemented until user accepts static appearance.

Exposed thigh band and long dark boots.

reviewHistory.summary: Initial clay geometry exists; Tier-1 rejected camera framing and narrow tail silhouette. Capture must use the reference portrait aspect and remove UI overlays before shape comparison. No visual acceptance granted.

Portrait capture now matches reference framing. Remaining silhouette mismatch is structural: twin tails widen too low and too thick, and legs remain parallel instead of converging. Replace generic neutral tail paths with measured reference row stations and restore observed standing silhouette; retain actual 3D thickness.

Reference-fitted closed-volume tail sections, sleeves and converging standing pose substantially improved the clay silhouette. Final deterministic IoU is 0.7915 versus required 0.85; aspect/scale pass. Face graphics, fringe, outfit details and colors are still future locked passes. Do not grant acceptance; another silhouette correction requires an explicit new correction budget.

lightingFromPhoto: Key light: broad upper-left soft white at [-3,6,5], intensity tuned in browser against palette.
Fill light: low-intensity neutral frontal fill [3,3,5], no ambient-only rendering.
Rim light: restrained cyan-white rear fill [2,5,-4] to show tail volume.
Exposure 1.0, neutral/ACES tone mapping chosen to preserve reference whites and teal; background neutral gray.
Contact shadow on subtle ground disc; character itself must remain separable from review background.
proceduralStrategy: Continuous parameterized ring-loft surfaces for head, torso, limbs and garment shells.
Closed volumetric ribbon lofts for bangs and flattened twin tails; smooth normals and embedded roots.
Flat stylized color regions, geometric trim and independent reference-derived facial albedo; no photographic grain invented.
risks: Reference alone does not determine rear geometry or exact depth.
Face texture and hair need close-up review; silhouette/global scores cannot establish eye or scalp correctness.
